title: fix(app-shell): a failed reaction write reverts and says so, instead of staying shown as applied (objectui#10899)
body:
Fixes #10899
Clause-②: no

This is the card's last open item, the one the epic PM's release comment 5869011976 left: `RecordDetailView`'s `handleToggleReaction` issued its `sys_comment` update from inside the state updater and discarded a rejected write, so a failed reaction stayed shown as applied. The card's other open items are carried elsewhere per 5865733451, 5865758466 and 5869011976: item 4 by objectui#10926, item 5b by objectui#10925 (merged) and objectstack-ai/cloud#2455.

Session `https://claude.ai/code/session_014mXUNuFomfj24w7s1pZzhN`, dispatch branch `claude/issue-10899-reaction-write-failure`, PM claim 5875254779. Base `ad0310fb57`, head `fd543fab66`.

## What changed

- `handleToggleReaction` now computes the toggle in the click handler, from the row on screen, with `toggleOwnReaction`. That is a pure module-level helper with the same four branches as before. It applies the toggle with a pure updater and issues the one `update` from the handler. The write no longer runs inside `setFeedItemsByRecord`.
- A refused write rolls the row back (see below) and raises `toast.error(t('detail.reactionFailed'))`. The key sits beside `detail.commentFailed` in all ten packs, each with a real translation. The English value is "Your reaction was not saved. Please try again."
- A resolved write keeps the toggle, as before.
- With no data source or no record key, the handler returns early: no write and no toast. Before this change, the no-data-source branch still toggled the row locally without writing. That branch has no rows to act on, because the feed is only read through a data source.
- The stored `{ emoji: userIds[] }` shape and its `__other__` padding are unchanged. The loop moved unchanged into `storedReactionShape`.
- Changeset: `@object-ui/app-shell` patch and `@object-ui/i18n` patch.

## Rollback: which one, and why

**Chosen: the snapshot option.** The row is restored to a recorded set only while it still shows the set this handler put there. The snapshot restored is the newest set that a write stored or may still store, not simply the set from before the click.

Each write stores the row's whole reaction set as of its click. After several quick clicks, the server therefore holds the set of the newest write it accepted. For each row, a small ledger records each click's set and how its write went. When a write is refused, the row shows the newest recorded set whose write was not refused; the set from before the first click is the stored floor. A refused click is taken back only when no later click, whose write carries it too, can still store it. If a re-read replaced the row in the meantime, the rollback is skipped, because the server copy is the truth. The error toast fires only when a rollback takes back something on screen.

Both plain options from the dispatch fail one of the pins below. I measured each as a one-off mutation of the `settle` function on the committed head, then restored it. After each restore, the blob hash equalled `HEAD` and `git diff HEAD` was empty.

| Pin | plain inverse toggle | plain snapshot, pre-click set | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| two clicks, both refused in click order | red: 2 toasts for one visible rollback (the display is right) | **red: shows `👍 2`, so the first refused click stays applied** | green |
| earlier refused, later stored | **red: shows `👍 1`, taking back a reaction the later write stored** | red: raises an error although nothing was lost | green |
| remove your own sole reaction, refused | red: the chip comes back last (`🎉 1, 👍 1`) | green | green |

Both options fail a card-direction case: a reaction is shown in a state the server does not hold. The plain snapshot fails in the most likely concurrent case, a tenant that refuses every write. The pinned rollback case is "two clicks, both refused". "Earlier refused, later stored" is the pin that tells this design apart from the plain inverse toggle.

## StrictMode measurement

I measured this rather than assuming it. On base `ad0310fb57`, the pin "under StrictMode, one click issues exactly one write" fails with `expected "vi.fn()" to be called 1 times, but got 2 times`. Under StrictMode, React's development build calls the updater twice, and the write lived in the updater. The console's `main.tsx` renders the app inside `React.StrictMode`, so a development console sent two updates per click. Production builds do not call updaters twice. On head the count is 1.

## Pins: red on base, green on head

The pins are in `RecordDetailView.reactionWriteFailure-10899.test.tsx`, next to item 2's `commentWriteFailure-10899` pins. They use the real `RecordDetailView`, `record:discussion` and `ReactionPicker`. Each `update` returns a promise that the case settles by hand. A chip is read as its emoji plus count; whether the reaction is the user's own is read from the emoji picker's `aria-selected`.

| Pin | kind | base `ad0310fb57` | head | ablation A: discarding catch back | ablation B: rollback ignores writes in flight |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| a rejected update puts the reaction back (count and own-mark) and raises the localized error, booted in zh: the toast is the zh catalogue entry, not the English one | fix | red | green | red | green |
| a second toggle before the first write settles, both rejected: both come off, one error | fix (the rollback case) | red | green | red | green |
| earlier rejected, later stored: both toggles stay, no error | choice pin | green | green | green | red |
| CONTROL: a resolved update keeps the toggle, no error | control | green | green | green | green |
| removing your own reaction, refused: it comes back in its place | control per the dispatch; red on base | red | green | red | green |
| under StrictMode, one click issues exactly one write | fix | red (2 writes) | green | green | green |

- Base: `Tests 4 failed | 2 passed (6)`. Head: `Tests 6 passed (6)`.
- Ablation A replaces the refusal branch `() => settle('failed')` with `() => {}`. Result: `3 failed | 3 passed`, exactly the three rows that depend on refusal handling. The StrictMode row stays green under A, because the write is still outside the updater; its red is in the base run.
- Ablation B replaces `find(s => s.outcome !== 'failed')` with `find(s => s.outcome === 'stored')`. Result: `1 failed | 5 passed`, exactly the choice pin.
- For each ablation, the anchor count was 1 before the change and 0 after, re-read from disk. Restore used `git checkout HEAD`, and the blob hash equalled `HEAD` afterwards.
- The dispatch called "removing your own reaction then failing restores it" a control. It is red on base, because base never restores, so it is listed here as a fix-direction row.

## Gates

- `@object-ui/app-shell` and `@object-ui/i18n` `type-check`: exit 0 at `fd543fab66`, after `turbo run build` of those two packages (29/29). Before that, the app-shell dependency closure was built (28/28). `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFiles` lists the new pin, 1 of 867 app-shell test files.
- Suite at `27df953e3e`: `vitest run --maxWorkers=2` over `packages/app-shell/`, `packages/i18n/` (which includes the pack parity suites) and the six tests outside those packages that import or read `RecordDetailView.tsx`. Result: `Test Files 945 passed | 1 skipped (946)`, `Tests 10130 passed | 22 skipped (10152)`, lock VERDICT command-exit 0. The only later commit, `fd543fab66`, changes comment lines only; the three feed-write pin files were re-run on it with `Tests 17 passed (17)`.
- At `fd543fab66`, all exit 0:
  - `check-changeset-presence`: 12 source files of 2 released packages, 1 changeset.
  - `check-changeset-no-major`.
  - `check:pending-changeset-literals`.
  - `check:new-line-citations`: `VERDICT new-cross-file-line-citations: 0 new citation(s)`.
  - `check:control-bytes`.
  - `check:i18n-keys` and `check:i18n-drift` (1 key added, 0 en values changed).
  - `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:vi-mock-override-shape` and `check:test-path-roots`.
- `check:changeset-claims` is report-only. It names two pending changesets that mention touched files: 6661, about strings under `console.nav` in `en.ts`, and 7997, prose about the DetailView retirement that names `RecordDetailView.tsx`. I read both paragraphs, and both are still true.
- Lint, narrowed to this diff: `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` over the 12 changed `.ts`/`.tsx` files. The config's `**/*.{ts,tsx}` block applies to all 12, and the JSON output reports 12 files.
  - `RecordDetailView.tsx`: 0 errors and 112 warnings at both base and head, with identical per-rule counts.
  - The new pin: 0 errors and 6 `no-explicit-any` warnings, the same fake-data-source casts the sibling pins use.
  - The packs: 0 errors, 0 warnings.
  - `eslint.config.js` sets no `parserOptions.project` or `projectService`, so type-aware linting is off and this diff cannot change the verdict on any untouched file. The repo-wide lint belongs to CI.
- Eager closure, from a console build at base and at head: 3,179,019 → 3,179,395 bytes gzipped, **+376**, with 330 eager chunks in both. The `RecordDetailView` chunk accounts for +319; the rest is ±1–8 bytes of chunk-hash reference churn. Base already fails the ceiling (`0.0 KB over the 3104.5 KB budget`, exit 1, objectui#10996), so `Bundle Analysis` will be red for that existing reason.
- `git merge-tree --write-tree` is clean, exit 0, against fresh `origin/main` `e9ca14ca93` and against PR objectui#11012's head `8fe632d960`. That PR's two citation-comment lines in the permission docblocks do not overlap this diff's handler hunk.

## Acceptance notes

- Out of scope, measured, not fixed, as the dispatch directs: every reaction write replaces other users' ids with `__other__`. In a one-off probe, the stored `{"👍":["u2","u3"]}` became `{"👍":["__other__","__other__"],"❤️":["u1"]}` after u1 added ❤️. So when u2 re-reads, their own 👍 no longer reads as theirs. This is the reaction-endpoint work the code comment names, and it is reported on the card.
- Not modeled, same as before: a server that applies an older reaction write after a newer one.
- A click in the moment between a rollback's state update and its render reads the row as it was before that render. Clicks are discrete events, so the window is one scheduler tick.
- NOT MEASURED: an in-browser check.
- Every build and test here ran under the shared verify lock.
